Study notes

The exams love numbers: days, dollar amounts and dimensions. These tables collect them by section of the CSLB outline.

LicensingFinancesEmploymentInsurance & liensContractsPublic worksSafetyGeneral Building

Law & Business · Licensing and business organization Chapter page →

TopicKey point
When a license is requiredLabor and materials of $1,000 or more (since 2025; previously $500)
Contractor bond$25,000; plus a $25,000 bond of qualifying individual when qualified by an RME
LLC requirements$100,000 employee/worker bond plus liability insurance (at least $1M for 5 or fewer personnel of record)
RMO / RMERMO is an officer, manager or member; RME is a W-2 employee working ≥ 32 hours a week or 80% of business hours
Qualifier leavesNotify and replace within 90 days or the license is suspended
RenewalActive license every 2 years; inactive every 4 years
Changes on recordReport name, address or personnel changes within 90 days
AdvertisingLicense number on business cards, vehicles, websites and all ads
Unlicensed workNo lawsuit to collect payment (B&P §7031) and no mechanics lien
Time to disciplineGenerally 4 years; 10 years for structural defects

Business finances Chapter page →

TopicKey point
Markup vs. marginMarkup is on cost, margin is on price: a 25% markup equals a 20% margin
Current ratioCurrent assets ÷ current liabilities; above 1 is generally wanted
Accrual vs. cashAccrual records revenue when earned; cash basis when money changes hands
Payroll taxesFUTA and California UI paid by employer; SDI withheld from employees; Social Security and Medicare split

Employment Chapter page →

TopicKey point
Form I-9Section 1 on day one; employer completes Section 2 within 3 business days
Overtime1.5× over 8 hours a day or 40 a week; 2× over 12 hours a day
Final payFired: immediately; quit without notice: within 72 hours
Meals and rest30-minute meal after 5 hours; 10-minute paid rest per 4 hours
Paid sick leaveAt least 40 hours or 5 days a year
New-hire reportTo EDD within 20 days (DE 34); I-9 Section 2 within 3 business days
Payroll recordsKeep at least 3 years
Employee vs. contractorCalifornia uses the ABC test; most construction workers are employees

Insurance and liens Chapter page →

TopicKey point
Preliminary noticeWithin 20 days of first furnishing labor or materials
Lien deadline (notice of completion recorded)Direct contractor 60 days; subcontractors and suppliers 30 days
Lien deadline (no notice of completion)90 days after completion
Workers' compensationRequired with employees; C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39 and D-49 need it even without employees; all contractors from 2028. EMR 1.0 is average, lower is better

Contracts Chapter page →

TopicKey point
Home improvement down payment$1,000 or 10% of the price, whichever is less
Right to cancel3 business days; 5 for owners 65 or older
Service and repair contractsSimplified rules at $750 or less
Change ordersIn writing, with the price effect, signed by both parties
Paying subcontractorsWithin 7 days of receiving a progress payment (B&P §7108.5)
Retention (private works)Capped at 5% for contracts from 2026 (Civil Code §8811); owner pays within 45 days of completion; prime pays subs within 10 days of receipt
Progress payments (private)Owner pays within 30 days of a written demand
Enforcing a lienNotice of completion recorded within 15 days of completion; sue within 90 days of recording the lien

Public works Chapter page →

TopicKey point
DIR registrationRequired before bidding, renewed yearly
Prevailing wageApplies over $1,000; submit certified payroll
Payment bondRequired on contracts over $25,000
ApprenticesRequired on contracts of $30,000 or more
Retention and payment5% cap; released within 60 days of completion, then to subs within 7 days
Subcontractor listingList subs over one-half of 1% of the prime bid

Safety Chapter page →

TopicKey point
Serious injury reportTo Cal/OSHA within 8 hours
IIPPEvery employer needs a written Injury and Illness Prevention Program
Tailgate meetingsAt least every 10 working days
AsbestosCal/OSHA registration for 100 sq ft or more
TrenchesProtective system at 5 ft or deeper; daily inspection by a competent person
Call 811At least 2 working days and no more than 14 calendar days before digging
HeatShade above 80°F; 1 quart of water per worker per hour
Fall protectionGenerally 7.5 ft in California construction (6 ft federal)

General Building (B) Chapter page →

The B exam leans residential and wood-frame: framing, seismic hardware, stucco and finishes are over 40% together. Contractors who mostly build steel and industrial work should study these closely.

SectionTopicKey point
PlanningConcrete volumeL × W × T (ft) ÷ 27 = cubic yards; order 5–10% extra
PlanningRoofing square1 square = 100 sq ft
PlanningRebar size#n = n/8 inch; #4 = ½ inch
Core tradesConcreteDesign strength at 28 days; slump measures workability; 3 in cover against earth
Core tradesElectrical14 AWG for 15 A, 12 AWG for 20 A; GFCI in baths, kitchen counters, garages, outdoors
Core tradesPlumbing¼ in per ft slope for drains 3 in and smaller; vents protect trap seals; two seismic straps on water heaters
FramingAnchor bolts½ in, ≤ 6 ft apart, within 12 in of plate ends; treated sill plates on concrete
FramingTop platesDoubled, joints offset ≥ 24 in
FramingStairs and guardsRiser ≤ 7¾ in, tread ≥ 10 in; guards 36 in residential, 42 in commercial
FramingStuccoScratch → brown → finish
Finish tradesGypsum boardType X fire-rated; MR moisture-resistant
Finish tradesEgress windows5.7 sq ft net (5.0 at grade floor); sill ≤ 44 in
Finish tradesCeilings and alarmsHabitable rooms ≥ 7 ft; smoke alarms in bedrooms, outside sleeping areas, every story
SafetyLadders and trafficExtension ladders 3 ft above landing; flaggers use STOP/SLOW paddles

References: CSLB Law & Business study guide · CSLB General Building study guide · CSLB California Contractors License Law & Reference Book.
